implementation_notes: Go has no inheritance, so the base action becomes middleware: an ordered chain of wrappers around http.Handler that performs authentication, authorization, session validation, input verification and audit before delegating to the business handler, composed once at the router and applied to every route tree. The shared sequence lives in the wrappers, the enforcers are ordinary functions or small types, and handlers stay free of security code. net/http itself provides only the Handler interface, so the disciplined wrapper chain is a local idiom rather than a framework feature.
pitfalls: Handlers registered directly on the mux bypass the chain; wrap once at the root or assert in tests that every registered route is wrapped.
The wrapper order is the security order, and a wrapper added last receives the request first; build the chain in one place and document the order.
Request-scoped identity must travel through context.Context with typed keys; package-level variables leak between goroutines.
